output.review_comment:
Functionally, this fix does make the full test suite pass (I traced all 10 cases by hand), and it correctly adds the missing `slot_minutes` divisor check and the 24:00→00:00 wraparound that the old formula lacked. So on the "make tests green without editing tests" mandate, it succeeds.

However, there's a real correctness/documentation problem the PR introduces (or rather, fails to reconcile): the docstring still says

> "a time exactly halfway between two boundaries rounds up to the later one"

but the new implementation uses Python's built-in `round()`, which is round-half-to-even ("banker's rounding"), not round-half-up. You can see this directly in the two tie-case tests:

- `snap_to_slot("08:45", 30) == "09:00"` — here 17.5 rounds to even index 18 → up. This happens to match the "rounds up" wording.
- `snap_to_slot("09:15", 30) == "09:00"` — here 18.5 also rounds to even index 18 → **down**, since 18 is already even. This directly contradicts the "rounds up to the later one" docstring text — 09:15 is exactly halfway between 09:00 and 09:30, yet the spec test wants it snapped down, not up.

So the tests actually encode round-half-to-even tie-breaking, not round-half-up, and the new code correctly implements that — but the docstring was left unchanged and now actively misdescribes the behavior. A future reader (or another agent) trusting the docstring will write code assuming ties always round up, and will be surprised in exactly the cases like `09:15`/30-min slots.

Please update the docstring to accurately describe the real tie-breaking rule (round-half-to-even) instead of leaving the "rounds up to the later one" claim, which is now false for roughly half of all tie cases. This is a doc fix, not a test change, so it doesn't run afoul of "don't change the tests."

Minor: the PR description is empty — worth a sentence summarizing the divisor check, wraparound fix, and the round-half-to-even behavior so reviewers don't have to reverse-engineer it as I did here.
